goal: Replace the rejected implicit-fragment callback with one exact manual six-digit invitation-code contract that preserves literal zero URL retention and the existing first-admin identity boundary.

decision.source: Q explicit selection after measured Chrome diagnostic retention
decision.supersedes: the implicit success/error fragment contract in onboarding commit 217e752 and n03-frontend-invite-contract-result.json

groundedProviderFacts: Supabase official email-template documentation says {{ .Token }} is a six-digit OTP usable instead of {{ .ConfirmationURL }} and recommends a clean custom link plus email/token verification.
Installed @supabase/auth-js 2.116.0 defines VerifyEmailOtpParams as { email, token, type: EmailOtpType } and EmailOtpType includes invite.

GoTrueClient.verifyOtp accepts user-supplied email OTP and type invite; GoTrueAdminApi states inviteUserByEmail does not support PKCE because invitation issuance and acceptance often use different browsers.
Current first-admin issuer already passes redirect_to equal to the exact signed clientOrigin /auth/invite and reads mailer_otp_exp while enforcing disable_signup=true.

sourceState.frontendWip: nine modified unstaged files from the blocked fragment implementation; preserve and revise in place, never reset/stash/clean

contractRequirements: The invite email contains a clean link to {{ .RedirectTo }} and visibly displays {{ .Token }}. It must not include ConfirmationURL, TokenHash, access/refresh token, email, marker or any credential in a URL. The configured redirect remains the exact signed clientOrigin /auth/invite.

The /auth/invite page starts with one form for email, six-digit ASCII code, new password and confirmation. Inputs are uncontrolled, email uses autocomplete=email, code uses autocomplete=one-time-code and inputMode=numeric, password fields use autocomplete=new-password. FormData is read only on submit and sensitive inputs are reset before awaiting Auth.

Before any Auth request, reject a nonempty query or fragment after synchronously removing it from the visible URL. Clean navigation itself carries no credential, so Chrome diagnostic metadata contains only /auth/invite.
Use the one existing CloudAuth/Supabase client with persistSession=false and detectSessionInUrl=false. If an ordinary current session exists, do not consume the OTP; return invite_session_conflict.

Call verifyOtp({ email: normalizedEmail, token: sixDigitCode, type: 'invite' }). Require a returned session/user with a nonblank provider subject and returned normalized email equal to the entered email. Do not decode JWTs or put email/code/session/subject in React state or errors.

Keep invite mode locked during verifyOtp and password update so auth events cannot expose getToken, run inspect, open VerifiedSession or call business APIs. Then call updateUser({ password }) in the same submit flow.

If password policy rejects after OTP success, retain only the in-memory invite session and show a password-only retry form; the consumed email/code are discarded. If the page reloads before password completion, return to the email/code form and require a new provider code when the old code is no longer valid. No browser persistence is added.

After confirmed password update, best-effort local-scope signout and mandatory local disposal produce complete. Success still means only Auth acceptance/password set; installer resume separately observes the private marker and binds users.auth_subject.

Keep provider failure redaction and the existing safe states where meaningful. Define exact local validation, expiry, session-conflict, password-rejected and provider-unavailable transitions; remove fragment-only invite_missing behavior if it no longer has an observable contract.
Keep the approved fail-closed staff browser cutover: no public signUp, no raw CCC invite link, no public staff accept client; participant request links remain unchanged.
Current N03 implementation is synthetic only. Auth template mutation, credential injection, live invite, deployment and operational acceptance remain separately unapproved.
